SMTO-SKL-0123 — This Slack request needs a connection made with your own account

GUID: 54796c47-0e84-5f69-bfaa-830534050e57
Slug: slack-principal-unsupported
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The Slack connection being used is the wrong kind for this request. For example, searching Slack messages only works through your personal Slack account, not a bot. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to list your Slack workspaces and check whether one is connected as a user (your personal account) rather than a bot. Message search and some other Slack requests only work through a personal account connection.
  2. If none is, open Parameter Store and add a Slack OAuth App entry that uses the user flow with search:read. Then ask the Agent to connect it under a new workspace key. A bot connection can't be turned into a personal one, so the personal account needs its own connection.
  3. Ask the Agent to repeat your request using the personal connection's workspace key. When you have several Slack connections, SMTO needs you to say which one to use.

What success looks like

  • The request returns results through your personal Slack connection.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Slack app. If your Slack workspace doesn't allow personal app connections, ask your Slack admin; SMTO can't search Slack through a bot.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected slack_workspace principal type is not supported by this method (search_messages requires a user principal), or Slack returned not_allowed_token_type.

What this means

  • Message search selects a non-user principal, or Slack reports not_allowed_token_type. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Message search selects a non-user principal, or Slack reports not_allowed_token_type.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect principal_type and the method's explicit supported principal contract.

How to fix it

  • Select a workspace_ref whose principal_type is user and whose granted_scopes include search:read (for search_messages), or connect one through a Slack OAuth App profile with flow "user" and requested_user_scopes containing search:read. Bot tokens are never swapped automatically.
  • Select an explicitly authorized principal supported by this Slack method. Message search requires a user token with search:read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately selected supported principal has the required scopes.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
